Accept existing findings with a baseline.
Read the reports the workflow leaves behind.
Send the recurring digest to Slack or Teams.
Offer the per-repository starter from the organization's
Open adoption pull requests at scale (optional).

The scan itself stays local. The organization-scan workflow lists repositories and downloads artifacts through the GitHub API; each scan checks out one repository and reads its files and Offing's bundled data, with no network access. Per-repository adoption uses one

Add one workflow to the caller repository. It calls

, which lists the organization's repositories and scans each one in a bounded matrix through the first-party Offing Action. The Action version follows the workflow tag you call, so pinning the workflow pins the scanner.

name: Offing organization scan

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 4 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  # Only needed for the Slack/Teams digest. Remove it if you do not post one.
  actions: read

jobs:
  org-scan:
    uses: velella-sh/offing/.github/workflows/org-scan.yml@v0.8.0
    with:
      organization: your-org
      fail-on-severity: high
      max-jobs: 10
    secrets:
      github-token: ${{ secrets.OFFING_ORG_TOKEN }}
      slack-webhook-url: ${{ secrets.OFFING_SLACK_WEBHOOK }}   # optional
      teams-webhook-url: ${{ secrets.OFFING_TEAMS_WEBHOOK }}   # optional
Commit it, then run it once by hand:

gh workflow run offing-org-scan.yml --repo your-org/your-ops-repo
gh run list --repo your-org/your-ops-repo --workflow offing-org-scan.yml --limit 1
gh run watch <run-id> --repo your-org/your-ops-repo

3. Accept existing findings with a baseline

A baseline records findings you have reviewed and accepted. It is usually a file committed in each repository. Findings in the baseline are suppressed; findings that are not in it are reported and gated normally.
Run this in the repository whose findings you are accepting:
The second command writes one entry per current finding and keeps the file's history when it already exists, so running it again updates the file instead of starting over:

Wrote 5 findings to /path/to/repository/.offing-baseline.json
No earlier baseline to compare with.
Review the file, then commit it:

git add .offing-baseline.json
git commit -m "chore: accept current Offing findings"
A scan that uses the baseline now hides exactly those findings:

Findings: 0
...
Baseline: 5 findings suppressed, 0 expiring within 14 days, 0 expired.
Add an owner, a reason, and an expiry

The baseline only takes effect where a workflow passes it to the Action or the reusable workflow. Prefer one
line that calls the reusable workflow:

jobs:

    uses: velella-sh/offing/.github/workflows/offing-reusable.yml@v0.8.0

      baseline: .offing-baseline.json
      fail-on-severity: high
Or pass the same inputs on the Action step directly:

- uses: velella-sh/offing@v0.8.0
  with:
    baseline: .offing-baseline.json
    fail-on-severity: high

Each scan job writes a versioned JSON report and uploads it as an artifact named
In GitHub, open the run from

From a terminal, download every report from a run and merge them into one organization view:

gh run list --repo your-org/your-ops-repo --workflow offing-org-scan.yml --limit 1
gh run download <run-id> --repo your-org/your-ops-repo \
  --pattern 'offing-report-*' --dir org-reports
npx @velella/offing rollup org-reports/*/offing-report.json
The rollup reads the saved reports and nothing else, so it uses no network and does not touch the repositories. It prints totals, then counts grouped by repository, product, and owner:

Offing rollup: 7 findings across 2 repositories

By repository:
  sample-api: 5 (2 high, 3 medium; nearest deadline 2020-02-11)
  sample-web: 2 (2 high; nearest deadline 2024-07-24)

By product:
  nodejs: 3 (3 medium) in sample-api
  github-actions: 2 (2 high) in sample-api, sample-web
  npm: 2 (2 high) in sample-api, sample-web

By owner:
  unowned: 7 (4 high, 3 medium) in sample-api, sample-web

7. Open adoption pull requests at scale

The organization-scan workflow covers every repository on a schedule. To put a pull-request workflow in every repository without waiting for each team to open the gallery, Offing can open the adoption pull requests for you. Offing lands best as one reviewed change per repository. The rollout tool (

) turns that into a single step: it lists the target repositories, shows exactly what it would change, and only opens pull requests when you explicitly ask for it. Nothing is ever pushed directly to a default branch, and scans stay offline: the tool's own network calls are GitHub API calls, never repository analysis.
Run it from a checkout of this repository:

npm ci
npm run org:rollout -- --org my-org                    # print the plan, change nothing
npm run org:rollout -- --org my-org --apply            # open one pull request per repository
npm run org:rollout -- --repos acme/api,acme/web       # a specific repository list instead of an org
with write access to the target repositories. A token with read-only access can still run the dry run.

GitHub Actions caps a matrix at 256 jobs, so an organization with more than 256 scannable repositories (archived and disabled repositories are skipped) needs call sites split into batches; call the workflow once per sub-organization. Archived and disabled repositories are skipped; forks and internal repositories are scanned unless the token cannot read them.
